question.worked_solution:
First, we clear the rational expressions by multiplying both sides of the inequality by the lowest common positive multiple of the denominators:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2a-4}{8} & \le \frac{2a}{6} \\ 24\cdot (\frac{2a-4}{8}) & \le 24\cdot (\frac{2a}{6}) \\ 3\cdot (2a-4) & \le 4\cdot 2a \\ 6a-12 & \le 8a\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the addition and multiplication principles. 

Remember, when we divide an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}6a-12 & \le 8a \\ 6a-12-8a & \le 8a-8a \\ -12-2a & \le 0 \\ -12-2a+12 & \le 0+12 \\ -2a & \le 12 \\ \frac{-2a}{-2} & \,\,\ge \,\,\frac{12}{-2} \\ a & \ge -6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $a\ge -6.$
